title: Aniimo Emberpup Fire Family | Scorchhowl vs Inferlupa, Evolution and Stats | Aniimo Guide
description: The Aniimo Emberpup line explained: Emberpup, Flameruff, Scorchhowl and Inferlupa. Evolution levels, stones, skills, base stats and which branch to pick, checked against aniimo.gg, Dexerto and AllThingsHow in November 2026.
joke: Choosing between Scorchhowl and Inferlupa is like choosing between two dinners, and then your Flameruff looks at you like it already picked.

sections.heading: Intro
sections.script: The Emberpup family is the very first entry in the Aniilog, and it is also the first one that makes you take a real decision. A small fire pup grows into Flameruff, and then the line splits in two. One branch is Scorchhowl, a fire fighter that wants to hit things hard. The other is Inferlupa, a three headed fire and dark wolf that breaks enemy guards. In this video we go through the whole family step by step. You will hear where to find Emberpup, what level and unlock each evolution needs, the base stats of every stage, the skills that matter and which branch fits which kind of team. The numbers come from aniimo.gg, the Dexerto Aniimo wiki and AllThingsHow, checked in November 2026. Where the sites disagree, we keep it simple and stay with what they share. Stay until the end, because the last section gives you a clear pick.

sections.heading: Meet Emberpup
sections.script: Emberpup is Aniilog number one, a stage one fire Aniimo. It is lively and energetic and likes to follow Flameruffs around. It is small, about nought point nine metres tall and twelve kilograms, and its base stats are modest, with sixty seven HP and ninety attack. Its fire element makes it strong against Grass and Ice, but it takes extra damage from Water and Earth, so remember that when you meet wet or rocky opponents. Its starting skills are simple but useful. Fire Bolt launches a fireball and stacks a fire debuff, Fire Kick is a dodge attack that dives down in a ring of flames, and Pebble Kick is an Earth dodge attack that can lock enemies in place. At home, an Emberpup can do Fire work and Hauling work, which makes it a handy helper even before it evolves.

sections.heading: Where to find it
sections.script: Emberpup is easy to meet. It is also one of the most common Aniimo in the world, with hundreds of wild spawn points on the map. The low level spot is Nimbus Fields, where wild Emberpup are around level five to fifteen, so that is the place for a new Pathfinder. Later areas have tougher ones. In The Argent Strait they are around level twenty eight to thirty two, in Beast Fang Ridge thirty to thirty five, in The Mistwoods around thirty five to thirty seven, and in Echoback Landing thirty six to forty. There is also a Highland form that adds a second element and lives in Russet Highlands and Zephyrus Landbridge at much higher levels, roughly forty five and above. Flameruff also spawns in the wild in several of the same areas, so if you find one at the right level you can skip the first evolution completely.

sections.heading: Emberpup to Flameruff
sections.script: The first evolution is the friendly one. Emberpup evolves into Flameruff at Aniimo level twelve, and you need to clear Sanctum First Spark to unlock it. Nothing else is listed as a cost, so there is no stone to hunt for. Flameruff is a stage two fire Aniimo, about one point two metres tall and eighteen kilograms. Its stats climb nicely, with eighty five HP and one hundred eleven attack, and its Fire work at home goes up too. It keeps the whole Emberpup skill kit, so Fire Bolt, Fire Kick and Pebble Kick all come along. This is a pack creature that prizes loyalty. Its description says it guards the younger Emberpup, and it is the stage where your plan matters, because Flameruff is the only one of the family that can take either of the two stage three exits.

sections.heading: The big split
sections.script: Here is the part people get wrong. Inferlupa is not a fourth stage hiding behind Scorchhowl. Both Scorchhowl and Inferlupa are parallel branches out of Flameruff, and Inferlupa only has number four in the Aniilog because of how the list is ordered. One Flameruff can only take one of the two exits, and there is no path from one stage three to the other. If you want both in your collection, raise two Flameruffs. Both exits need Aniimo level twenty, but the unlocks are different. Scorchhowl is unlocked by defeating the Alpha Scorchhowl and needs a Blaze Stone. Inferlupa is unlocked by completing Journey Warrior and needs a Night Stone plus six Unbroken Flameruff Spirits. Collect everything first, and only then commit your level twenty Flameruff.

sections.heading: Scorchhowl the fighter
sections.script: Scorchhowl is the straightforward branch. It stays pure fire in the data we checked, it is a damage dealer, and it stands one point seven metres tall and weighs twenty five kilograms. Its base stats show a big jump, with ninety five HP, one hundred nineteen attack, eighty physical defence, seventy five magic defence and ninety regen. It also gets three new skills. Burn Breaker is a charged blast with power eighty four that costs thirty energy and does extra damage for energy spent at full charge. Falling Star is the ultimate, a flaming slam on a wide area with power one hundred seventy. Lightning Kick is an electric dodge attack that can paralyse on a successful dodge. Scorchhowl also appears wild in Beast Fang Ridge at levels thirty to thirty five, along with its Thunderstorm and Prismana forms, so you can also catch one directly.

sections.heading: Inferlupa the breaker
sections.script: Inferlupa is a fire and dark wolf with the Break role. Its stats show what it is built for. Break is one hundred eight, compared with fifty two on Scorchhowl, and its regen is ninety nine, the highest in the family, so it can keep casting. Attack is lower at eighty nine, and physical defence is seventy. Its basic attack switches to darkness. Its trait is Full Energy, which triggers after eight basic attacks. In that state Unbroken Flameruff Spirit bounces seven times instead of five, Hunting Pack summons an extra clone, Blazing Wolf Assault adds a clone with super armour, and Crossfire gains forty five percent might. Wolfpack Onslaught, the ultimate, has power one hundred ninety four and costs no energy. Because it is part dark, it takes extra damage from Light and Wind, so keep that in mind.

sections.heading: Which branch to pick
sections.script: So which one should you raise? Look at your team. If you already have plenty of damage but struggle to break enemy guards, Inferlupa is the branch that changes the fight. Its Break stat and its skills that stack Break efficiency are built for that job, and it does both Fire and Dark work at home. If you simply want a clean fire attacker, Scorchhowl is the cleaner upgrade, with the highest attack and defence of the two and a huge ultimate. Scorchhowl is also easier to get, because you can raise it from Flameruff or catch it wild. The cost is the other point. Inferlupa needs those six spirits and a Night Stone, so it takes more planning. Remember the element chart too. Fire hits Grass and Ice for one point six times damage, but Water and Earth hit fire back hard, so pair these two with a teammate that covers those weaknesses.

sections.heading: Your plan
sections.script: Here is a simple plan. Catch an Emberpup in Nimbus Fields, clear Sanctum First Spark and take it to level twelve for Flameruff. Keep going to level twenty, and do not evolve yet. Decide first. If you want Scorchhowl, defeat the Alpha Scorchhowl, bring a Blaze Stone and evolve. If you want Inferlupa, finish Journey Warrior, gather the Night Stone and six Unbroken Flameruff Spirits, and then evolve. Or catch a second Emberpup and do both. Whichever you pick, the family is one of the best ways to learn how Aniimo evolution, roles and elements work. Which branch will you raise first, Scorchhowl or Inferlupa? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe to HarryBeast Gaming for more Aniimo guides every day.
